Choosing courses

WGU single courses: what the $25 price includes and when costs rise

WGU currently advertises heavily discounted single courses from $25, while its November 2026 institutional catalog lists substantially higher single-course rates. Check that you qualify for the advertised offer and confirm the checkout price, access period and automatic subscription before choosing it for a degree plan.

Identify the exact product and access period

WGU’s current single-course page advertises most individual courses at $25 for an initial two-month term. IT and Technology Fundamentals is listed at $49 for three months, and selected two-course bundles start at $49. Its FAQ describes the prices as heavily discounted. Access includes learning materials and electronic textbooks. These are advertised single-course offers, not a WGU bachelor’s degree term.

The current November 2026 institutional catalog, printed page 51, separately lists single courses at $750–$1,000 for two to three months and bundles at $1,500–$1,750 for three to four months. The live pages do not establish the exact eligibility boundary reconciling those rates with the advertised discounts. Do not assume every learner or checkout qualifies for $25 or $49. Obtain the offer and applicable terms for your course before treating a discounted scenario as your budget.

After the initial term, the standard offering automatically transitions to a $99 monthly subscription that can be canceled. There is an important exception: the PACA and IT and Technology Fundamentals bundle lists a $199 monthly subscription. Read the actual checkout and cancellation terms for the selected product rather than applying the standard $99 amount to every bundle.

Calculate initial access plus any extension months

If you qualify for an advertised standard $25 course, the arithmetic is $25 plus $99 for each paid extension month. Zero, one and two extension months produce $25, $124 and $223 in course-access charges. These examples assume that specific advertised offer and exclude any unlisted personal or receiving-school expense. They do not establish discount eligibility or predict how long you will need.

For the $49 IT and Technology Fundamentals individual course, the initial three-month term plus one standard $99 extension would be $148. A $49 two-course bundle is a shared purchase; do not charge the full bundle twice when comparing its two courses. Check its exact initial duration and renewal before using it in a personal budget.

Conditional advertised-offer scenarios using the standard $99 monthly extension; verify discount eligibility and checkout terms. Not the $199 exception bundle or a completion forecast.

Financial aid for WGU degree programs does not apply to these single-course purchases; WGU says federal aid is unavailable for the offering.

Separate WGU credit from the receiving school’s award

WGU says completed single courses appear on an official WGU transcript. That is useful evidence about the issuer, but an outside receiving institution decides whether to accept the course, its equivalent and its placement. WGU competency units should remain identifiable; do not silently label every unit a semester or quarter credit.

Before purchase, send your destination the exact source code, syllabus, competency units and intended degree requirement. WGU’s catalog explicitly distinguishes standalone course numbers from degree-course numbers; matching titles or removing a code suffix does not establish equivalency. Ask about the required result, transcript and duplication policy. A course accepted as a general elective may do little for a degree whose electives are already complete. A collection of inexpensive university courses is not automatically a mapped 10- or 20-course transfer pathway.

For a WGU degree goal, use the particular degree’s transfer and admission rules and have the official evaluation completed. A single-course purchase does not itself establish full degree admission. Keep WGU-taught coursework separate from ACE-recommended provider learning when the receiving policy distinguishes those sources.

Choose by the actual assessments, not the self-paced label

The syllabi linked from WGU’s official page show why assessments must be checked course by course. Applied Algebra C957A and Organizational Behavior C715A each list three competency units and a final assessment; both explicitly require at least one proctored test, an external webcam and the Guardian browser. They should not be offered as non-proctored options.

English Composition I, identified as ENG in its linked ENG101-path syllabus, instead lists four papers for three competency units. Introduction to Communication: Connecting with Others D268A lists three final projects for three competency units. These are useful examples for a learner who prefers written or project work, but the examples do not prove that every course or later revision uses the same format.

Allow time for writing, revision and evaluation when comparing the initial access window with the subscription. Check technical requirements, accessibility arrangements and the current syllabus before paying. A low course price is less useful if its assessment format prevents you from completing it.

Check eligibility and the next step separately

WGU markets this offering without requiring full degree admission. Its course list still includes specific restrictions: Learners and Learning Science is marked for students who already hold a bachelor’s degree, and nursing-related pathways include state and prelicensure eligibility conditions. Do not generalize one course’s eligibility to the entire list or treat a nursing preparation course as admission to a nursing degree.

The useful purchase decision has four parts: you qualify for the selected course, its assessment format works for you, your destination confirms a useful placement, and your budget accounts for access beyond the introductory period. Keep copies of the offer, syllabus, evaluation and final record so a later course-page change does not rewrite what you actually completed.

Review the single-course source profile

Compare WGU’s current advertised offer, unresolved eligibility and specific assessments before choosing an individual course. The profile does not establish a receiving-school match.
